title: **They were dying… and the cure sounded too simple.**
paragraphs: **They were dying… and the cure sounded too simple.**
Imagine the scene.

Dust.
Panic.
Screams echoing through the camp of Israel.

Men clutching their legs.
Women collapsing into the sand.
Children crying as the venom spreads through their veins.
Serpents everywhere.
Not harmless snakes.

**Fiery serpents.**
Burning bites.
Poison racing through blood like wildfire.
This wasn’t just a bad day in the wilderness.
This was judgment.

Because the people who were rescued by God…
the people who saw the Red Sea split…
the people who ate bread from heaven…
**turned their hearts against Him.**

They complained.
They despised the manna.
They accused God of bringing them out to die.
Numbers 21 tells us the truth we often try to hide:

**Sin is not small.
And rebellion always carries venom.**
So the serpents came.
And suddenly the camp realized something terrifying:
**they could not save themselves.**

No medicine.
No strategy.
No strength strong enough to stop the poison already spreading inside them.
Sound familiar?
Because the Bible says humanity is facing the same crisis.
Not snake venom…
**sin venom.**
It moves through the soul quietly.

It poisons relationships.
It corrodes truth.
It slowly kills hope.

Religion can’t cure it.
Self-improvement can’t cure it.
Good intentions can’t cure it.
The human heart has been bitten.
And we are dying.
But then—right in the middle of judgment—something shocking happens.
God provides a remedy.
Not a complicated ritual.
Not a heroic test of strength.
Something almost offensively simple.
God tells Moses:

> “Make a fiery serpent and set it on a pole, and everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.”
> — Numbers 21:8
Let that sink in.
The very symbol of the curse…
**lifted up.**
And the cure?
**Look.**
That’s it.

No climbing the pole.
No paying a price.
No proving worthiness.
Just look.
Imagine a dying man in the sand.

His breathing shallow.
Vision fading.
Someone shouts:
“LOOK! The bronze serpent!”

And with the last strength he has…
he lifts his eyes.
And the poison loses its power.
Life returns.
Healing floods his body.
Not because bronze has magic.
But because **God attached His promise to the lifted sign.**
And then—centuries later—Jesus drops a thunderbolt of revelation.
He says:

> “Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up.”
> — John 3:14
Do you see it?
The wilderness was pointing to **the cross.**
Humanity was bitten by sin.
And the cure would not come through human effort.
It would come through **a Savior lifted up.**
Jesus Christ.
The sinless Son of God.
Nailed to a Roman cross outside Jerusalem.
The innocent One carrying the curse of the guilty.
The Holy One standing where sinners should stand.
So that anyone—anyone—who looks to Him in faith…
**will live.**
Not because we deserve it.
Not because we earned it.
But because grace is stronger than venom.
Listen carefully.
Some people try to outrun their sin.
Others try to hide it.
Others try to bury it under good works.
But the Gospel says something radically different.

**Stop running.
Stop pretending.
Stop trying to heal yourself.**
Look.
Look to the One who was lifted up.
Look to Jesus.
Because the cross is not just a symbol of suffering.
It is the place where poison loses its power.
The place where shame breaks.
The place where sinners find mercy.
Maybe you feel the venom today.

Regret.
Addiction.
Hidden compromise.
A past that whispers, “You’re too far gone.”
But hear this clearly:
**No one who looked at the bronze serpent died.**
And no one who truly looks to Christ will be turned away.
Not the broken.
Not the ashamed.
Not the person who thinks their story is already ruined.
The cross still stands.
The Savior is still lifted up.
And grace is still flowing.
So here is the question that echoes from the wilderness to the cross to this very moment:
**Where are you looking?**
At your failure?
At your fear?
At the poison in your past?
Or at the Savior who conquered it all?
Today the invitation is simple.
Not easy for pride.
But simple.
**Look… and live.**
Look to Jesus.
Look to the cross.
Look to the One who died and rose again.
And discover what millions across history have discovered:
The venom of sin is real.
But the grace of Christ is stronger.
Someone in your circle might be dying from a wound they think no one sees.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
